name: Loktak Lake
description: Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in north-east India, a broad stretch of water in Bishnupur district about 48 km from Imphal that resembles a miniature inland sea. It is famed for its phumdis, floating swamps of vegetation and soil on which fishermen live in huts called phumsangs, and it holds Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park.
how_to_reach: About 48 km from Imphal by road; the Sendra hillock gives an overview of the lake and has a tourist home with a cafeteria.
practical_notes: Boating and water sports are organised at the Takmu Water Sports Complex. Migratory birds are usually sighted from November to March.

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
description: Keibul Lamjao is the only floating national park in the world, sitting on the southern shore of Loktak Lake in Bishnupur district. The wetland is the last natural habitat of the endangered brow-antlered deer, the Sangai or dancing deer of Manipur, and supports a distinctive assembly of flora, waterfowl and other wildlife.
how_to_reach: About 50-55 km from Imphal, reached by road towards Moirang and then into the park area on the lake.
practical_notes: The Forest Department maintains watch towers and two rest houses. Migratory waterfowl are usually seen from November to March; keep a respectful distance from the Sangai.
address: Keibul Lamjao National Park, Bishnupur, Manipur

name: Sendra Island
description: Sendra is a hillock overlooking Loktak Lake near Phubala in Bishnupur district. It is the classic viewpoint over the lake, giving a bird's-eye view of the phumdis and the floating fishing huts, and has long been a favourite stop for visitors to the lake.
how_to_reach: Reached from the Tedim Road (NH 150) through Phubala, about 48 km from Imphal; the Sendra Tourist Home with an attached cafeteria stands at the viewpoint.
practical_notes: Boating can be arranged from the lakeside, and the hillock is the best place to take in the scale of the lake and its floating islands.

name: INA Memorial Complex, Moirang
description: At Moirang in Bishnupur district the flag of the Indian National Army was first unfurled on 14 April 1944, giving the town a special place in India's freedom struggle. The INA Memorial and museum hold photographs, letters, badges of rank and other war memorabilia recalling the sacrifices of the soldiers under Subhas Chandra Bose.
how_to_reach: Moirang town, Bishnupur district, about 48 km from Imphal on the Tiddim Road (NH 150).
practical_notes: Allow time for the museum as well as the memorial; the collection is the main reason to visit.
address: INA Memorial Complex, Moirang, Bishnupur, Manipur

name: Red Hill (Maibam Lokpaching) & India Peace Memorial
description: Red Hill at Maibam Lokpaching is a hillock about 16 km from Imphal where British and Japanese soldiers fought a fierce battle during the Second World War, with Japanese troops joining the Indian National Army. War veterans built the India Peace Memorial here in honour of the Japanese soldiers who died, and the site draws Japanese pilgrims.
how_to_reach: About 16 km from Imphal on the Tiddim Road (NH 150), at Maibam Lokpaching in Bishnupur district.
practical_notes: A place of pilgrimage for Japanese visitors; the memorial and the surrounding battlefield landscape are the main features.
address: Red Hill (Maibam Lokpaching) & India Peace Memorial, Bishnupur, Manipur

name: Takmu Water Sports Complex
description: The Takmu Water Sports Complex on Loktak Lake is the venue for the state's traditional water sports and hosts part of the annual Manipur Sangai Festival. Events include the local boat race, water skiing, motorboating and wind-surfing.
how_to_reach: On the Loktak lakefront in Bishnupur district, about 48 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: Water-sport activity is concentrated around festival time; check on the day for what is operating.
address: Takmu Water Sports Complex, Bishnupur, Manipur

name: Shri Gopinath Temple
description: The Shri Gopinath Temple at Ningthoukhong is the second largest temple in Manipur, a striking white structure that draws more than ten lakh devotees each year. Holi, Diwali, Janmashtami and Durga Pooja are celebrated here on a grand scale.
how_to_reach: At Ningthoukhong in Bishnupur district, about 35 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: The major Hindu festivals bring very large crowds; the temple is quieter on ordinary days.

name: Lakoi Pat (Loukoi Pat)
description: Lakoi Pat, also written Loukoi Pat, is a small lake beside the Tiddim Road in Bishnupur district. Official tourism material describes it as a retreat for visitors with boating facilities and considerable scenic charm.
how_to_reach: Near the Tiddim Road (NH 150) in Bishnupur district, a short stop on the Imphal-Moirang route.
practical_notes: A compact scenic stop rather than a full-day destination; boating is the main activity.

name: Kangla Fort
description: Kangla at the centre of Imphal is the most important historical and archaeological site in Manipur and a symbol of the state's heritage. It served as the royal palace from the time of Pakhangba and holds numerous holy shrines sacred to the Meitei, combining ancient fortifications with living religious traditions.
how_to_reach: In central Imphal city, Imphal West district; reached easily by city bus or taxi.
practical_notes: The site mixes archaeological remains with active shrines; allow at least an hour and dress modestly when entering temples.

name: Shaheed Minar
description: Shaheed Minar, the Martyrs' Memorial in Bir Tikendrajit Park, honours the Meitei and tribal martyrs who fought the British in 1891, including Crown Prince Bir Tikendrajit Singh. The monument is made up of three vertical beams joined at the top by three mythical dragons.
how_to_reach: In Bir Tikendrajit Park in the centre of Imphal city, Imphal West district.
practical_notes: It sits close to Kangla and the state museum, so the three can be visited together on foot or by short taxi rides.

name: Imphal War Cemetery
description: The Imphal War Cemetery is a poignant memorial to soldiers who died fighting Japanese forces in the Second World War. Maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission, it is the resting place of around 1,600 Commonwealth service personnel, with brass plaques recording the identities of the fallen.
how_to_reach: Within Imphal city in the Imphal East and West area, a short taxi ride from the centre.
practical_notes: A quiet commemorative site; a second Commonwealth war cemetery lies at Hatta Golapati and Kaboleikai in Imphal East.
address: Imphal War Cemetery, Imphal West, Manipur

name: Mapal Kangjeibung (World's Oldest Living Polo Ground)
description: Mapal Kangjeibung in Imphal is described as the world's oldest living polo ground. Modern polo traces its origins to the Manipuri game of Sagol Kangjei, played on the distinctive Manipuri pony as a test of royal martial and cavalry skill.
how_to_reach: In the centre of Imphal city, Imphal West district.
practical_notes: Matches and polo events are held here; check locally for a schedule if you want to see a game.
address: Mapal Kangjeibung (World's Oldest Living Polo Ground), Imphal West, Manipur

name: Ima Keithel (Ema Market)
description: Ima Keithel, the Khwairamband Bazar in central Imphal, is the world's only all-women market. More than 500 years old, it is run by around 3,000 Emas or mothers, and men are not permitted to sell goods there.
how_to_reach: Khwairamband Bazar in central Imphal, Imphal West district.
practical_notes: The market spreads over two sides of the road: vegetables, fruit, fish and groceries on one side, handlooms and household goods on the other.
address: Ima Keithel (Ema Market), Imphal West, Manipur

name: Shri Bijoy Govindaji Temple, Sagolband
description: The Shri Bijoy Govindaji Temple at Sagolband is regarded by many as the oldest temple in Manipur. Tradition holds that the elder brother of the deity worshipped at the Shree Shree Govindajee Temple resides here, and the two share architectural similarities.
how_to_reach: At Sagolband in Imphal city, Imphal West district.
practical_notes: A peaceful, less crowded temple where visitors are welcome to join daily devotional activities.
address: Shri Bijoy Govindaji Temple, Sagolband, Imphal West, Manipur

name: Khonghampat Orchidarium
description: The Khonghampat Orchidarium near Imphal is a 200-acre site holding more than 110 distinct orchid varieties. It is at its most colourful during the March-April blooming season, when the flowers and the surrounding views draw visitors.
how_to_reach: About 10 km from Imphal at Khonghampat, in Imphal West district.
practical_notes: The March-April bloom is the worthwhile window; outside it, much of the collection is not in flower.

name: Shree Shree Govindajee Temple
description: Shree Shree Govindajee Temple is the historic centre of Vaishnavism in Manipur. Its twin domes are covered with gold-plated sheets, and it has a paved courtyard and a large congregation hall; the presiding deity Radha-Krishna is carved from a jackfruit tree.
how_to_reach: Within Imphal city in Imphal East district, near the palace compound.
practical_notes: Devotees gather for daily worship and visitors can share in a vegetarian prasad meal at a nominal charge.
address: Shree Shree Govindajee Temple, Imphal East, Manipur

name: Mutua Museum
description: The Mutua Museum at Andro is a cultural complex holding artefacts from across north-east India, including rare coins, manuscripts, wood carvings and jewellery. Replicas of houses belonging to the region's different tribes and ethnic groups are a particular highlight.
how_to_reach: At Andro, about 26 km from Imphal in Imphal East district.
practical_notes: It pairs naturally with the Panam Ningthou Temple and Panam Eco-Park, which are in the same village area.

name: Panam Ningthou Temple
description: The village of Andro preserves a centuries-old tradition of continuously burning fire, regarded as the oldest man-made fire in India. The sacred flame is housed at the Panam Ningthou Temple and is cared for by the temple authorities, alongside the village's distinctive architecture.
how_to_reach: At Andro, about 26 km from Imphal in Imphal East district.
practical_notes: A heritage and religious site; follow any restrictions the temple authorities place on photography or access to the flame.
address: Panam Ningthou Temple, Imphal East, Manipur

name: Panam Eco-Park
description: The Panam Eco-Park at Andro surrounds the shrine known as Chakpa Panam Ningthou Meithoupirol Shanglen or Mei Mutaba, the fire that does not stop. The fire inside the old traditional temple is said to have burned for more than a thousand years, and the eco-park around it is a visitor hub.
how_to_reach: At Andro, about 23.7 km from Imphal in Imphal East district.
practical_notes: The site combines the eternal-fire shrine with an eco-park; Mutua Museum and Santhei Natural Park are nearby.

name: Marjing Polo Complex
description: The Marjing Polo Complex stands near the heritage shrine of Ibudhou Marjing at Heingang. Marjing is the deity of the Chenglei to whom the Kangjei, or polo stick, and the ball are still offered in worship, making the complex a natural centre for polo tourism.
how_to_reach: At Heingang, about 9 km from Imphal in Imphal East district.
practical_notes: The focus is Manipur's polo heritage and the adjoining Marjing hill shrine.
address: Marjing Polo Complex, Imphal East, Manipur

name: Santhei Natural Park
description: Santhei Natural Park at Andro is a community initiative, created by villagers to conserve nature and protect their culture, including a long-burning sacred ritual fire. A dam built at the site forms an artificial water source and adds to the scenery.
how_to_reach: At Andro, about 23.7 km from Imphal in Imphal East district.
practical_notes: A village-run conservation project; the dam and the sacred fire are the principal features.
address: Santhei Natural Park, Imphal East, Manipur

name: Shilheipung
description: Shilheipung is an eco-tourism centre in Imphal East district, set among paddy fields with a hill viewpoint over flowering landscapes. It is promoted for family outings, picnics, wood-crafting and relaxed walks in the surrounding countryside.
how_to_reach: Near Lamlai in Imphal East district, about 20 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: Geared to family visits, with picnics, craft activities and gentle walks rather than strenuous trekking.

name: Awunching Park (The Great Escape)
description: Awunching Park, promoted as The Great Escape, covers 367 hectares and was established in 2003. It offers active options such as paintball and water zorbing alongside quieter pastimes including painting and photography.
how_to_reach: In Imphal East district, about 14-15 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: Suits a range of ages; check which of the activities are running before you go.
address: Awunching Park (The Great Escape), Imphal East, Manipur

name: Manipur Adventure and Allied Sports Institute (MAASI)
description: The Manipur Adventure and Allied Sports Institute, or MAASI, was established in 1981 to promote adventure sports. Its 120-acre complex at Keirao supports training and treks, with jungle exploration, mountaineering and rock climbing among the activities on offer.
how_to_reach: At Keirao in Imphal East district, about 17 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: An adventure base rather than a casual sightseeing stop; contact the institute in advance about programmes.
address: Manipur Adventure and Allied Sports Institute (MAASI), Imphal East, Manipur

name: Khongjom War Memorial
description: The Khongjom War Memorial atop Kheba Hill commemorates Major General Paona Brajabashi and the Manipuri fighters who resisted the British army in the 1891 Anglo-Manipuri war. Khongjom Day is observed here each year on 23 April.
how_to_reach: At Khongjom in Thoubal district, about 36 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: The memorial stands on a hillock; the annual 23 April observance draws larger crowds.

name: Kaina Temple & Shri Bungshibudon Temple
description: Kaina Temple occupies a hillock held sacred by Hindus in Thoubal district and is a local centre of culture. The temple complex includes a revered jackfruit tree from which an idol is believed to have been carved; the Shri Bungshibudon Temple at nearby Khangabok is a few kilometres away.
how_to_reach: In Thoubal district, about 29 km from Imphal; Khangabok is a short distance further on.
practical_notes: Can be combined conveniently with MMRC Park at Khangabok.
address: Kaina Temple & Shri Bungshibudon Temple, Thoubal, Manipur

name: MMRC Park and Unity Park
description: MMRC Park at Khangabok is both a recreational park and a research centre. It represents the cultures of Manipur's ethnic groups with a focus on traditional Meitei structures such as Meetei Yumjao and the Pakhangba Temple, and has a children's park for family outings.
how_to_reach: At Khangabok in Thoubal district, about 27.2 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: A family-oriented site with recreated traditional structures and play facilities for children.
address: MMRC Park and Unity Park, Thoubal, Manipur

name: Waithou Lake
description: Waithou Lake is a broad waterbody near Waithou in Thoubal district, one of the valley's sizeable wetlands and a local scenic spot.
how_to_reach: Near Waithou in Thoubal district, a short drive out from Imphal by road.
practical_notes: A quieter lake setting best combined with other Thoubal district stops such as Khangabok and Kaina.

name: Kakching Garden
description: Kakching Garden lies at Uyok Ching, south of Kakching Bazar. Developed as a tourist centre, it includes the Mahadev Temple, Ibudhou Pakhang Laiseng, a statue of Hao Sampubi, a park and restaurants, with a rose garden as its showpiece.
how_to_reach: At Uyok Ching, south of Kakching Bazar in Kakching district, about 45 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: The rose garden is the main draw; the site also has temples, a statue and food outlets.

name: Shirui Hills
description: Shirui Hills in Ukhrul district is a scenic hilltop covered with wildflowers and the rare Shirui lily, Lilium mackliniae, the state flower of Manipur found only in the Siroy hill range. The hills are also noted for rare birds and wildlife.
how_to_reach: About 90 km from Imphal in Ukhrul district; the annual Shirui Lily Festival is held here in May.
practical_notes: The lilies bloom in May and June; the hilltop trek coincides with the peak flowering season.

name: Khangkhui Lime Caves
description: The Khangkhui lime caves in Ukhrul district are prehistoric sedimentary limestone caves lined with stalagmites and stalactites. Excavations have found evidence of Stone Age habitation, making the caves a drawing point for archaeologists and researchers as well as visitors.
how_to_reach: Near Khangkhui village in Ukhrul district, about 90 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: The caves are dark and uneven; carry a torch and wear shoes with good grip.

name: Phangrei
description: Phangrei is one of Manipur's hill stations, a peak that joins the Shirui range in Ukhrul district. It is noted for pristine scenery, rich flora and fruits, and a waterfall that cascades down the hill range.
how_to_reach: About 103 km from Imphal in Ukhrul district.
practical_notes: A day-trip hill destination; the waterfall and the surrounding flora are the main features.

name: Dzukou Valley
description: Dzukou Valley lies in Senapati district on the border with Nagaland and is one of Manipur's best-known trekking destinations. The valley is celebrated for its rolling green carpet of flora, including the rare Dzuko lily, and for sweeping landscapes that change with the seasons.
how_to_reach: About 82.8 km from Imphal in Senapati district, approached by a trek from the road head on the Manipur-Nagaland border.
practical_notes: The valley is at its best from late June to September, when the flowers and lily bloom; the terrain is exposed, so plan for changing weather.

name: Yangkhullen Village
description: Yangkhullen is a village built on a rocky slope in Senapati district, home to the Zeme community. The whole village lives together in a close-knit way, passing customs and traditions from one generation to the next, and it attracts historians and research scholars.
how_to_reach: About 135 km from Imphal in Senapati district.
practical_notes: A living traditional settlement; ask permission before entering homes or photographing residents.

name: Willong Khullen
description: Willong Khullen in Senapati district is known for ancient stone structures comparable to the stonehenges found elsewhere in the world. The site is still little visited and lies about 37 km from NH 39.
how_to_reach: About 37 km off NH 39 in Senapati district.
practical_notes: The megalithic stone structures are the reason to visit; expect limited facilities and check the approach locally.

name: Sadu Chiru Waterfall
description: Sadu Chiru is a perennial waterfall beside the Tiddim Road, with three falls in all and a drop officially described as roughly 300 metres. The approach crosses fields, streams and forest before a climb up stone steps to a view over the green valley below.
how_to_reach: About 20-25 km from Imphal beside the Tiddim Road (NH 150); official material variously places it in Kangpokpi and Senapati districts.
practical_notes: A short trek with a final stone-step climb; wear shoes with grip, particularly in wet weather.

name: Koubru Peak
description: Koubru is a prominent peak in the northern hills of Kangpokpi district, a landmark in the Meitei landscape and a seasonal destination for pilgrims and walkers.
how_to_reach: North of Imphal in Kangpokpi district; road access reaches the foothills, with the final ascent on foot.
practical_notes: Confirm trail and weather conditions locally before setting out; the climb is not a casual stroll.

name: Eco-Park, Thangal Surung
description: The eco-park at Thangal Surung in Kangpokpi district is the birthplace of the renowned General Thangal. It is laid out as a place for photography, picnics and paying respects to the general's memory.
how_to_reach: At Thangal Surung in Kangpokpi district, about 32.9 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: A low-key picnic and photography spot with a historical association.

name: Tharon Cave
description: Tharon Cave in Tamenglong district is a mystical cave of archaeological and historical importance, thought to have served as a shelter for thousands of years. Excavations inside produced objects linked to the Hobinian culture of North Vietnam.
how_to_reach: About 27 km from Tamenglong town, roughly 190 km from Imphal by road.
practical_notes: Largely undeveloped; carry a torch and take care on uneven ground.

name: Bunning Meadow
description: Bunning Meadow lies on the western side of Tamei town in Tamenglong district. In June the meadow fills with ground orchids and wild lilies, making it a favourite for nature lovers at that time of year.
how_to_reach: On the west side of Tamei in Tamenglong district, about 180 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: June is the month to see the orchids and lilies in bloom.

name: Zeilad Lake
description: Zeilad Lake is a hill-top lake in Tamenglong district that has been declared one of Manipur's wildlife sanctuaries. It supports a variety of fish and birds as well as pythons, and is a quiet scenic spot.
how_to_reach: In Tamenglong district, about 180 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: A sanctuary as well as a scenic lake; the wildlife, especially the birdlife, is the main interest.

name: Barak Waterfalls
description: Barak Waterfalls lie in the forest of Tamenglong district and are known for photography, picnics and adventure sports including rafting in the chilly hill water. The Barak river here is rich in aquatic biodiversity.
how_to_reach: In the forests of Tamenglong district, about 180 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: Rafting and water sports are the added attraction; the falls are a popular picnic destination.

name: Rani Gaidinliu Tomb
description: This memorial marks the resting place of Rani Gaidinliu, the Heraka leader honoured by Jawaharlal Nehru as the Daughter of the Hills for her resistance to British rule. It stands in the Nungkao or Longkao area of Tamenglong district, associated with the last phase of her life.
how_to_reach: In the Nungkao/Longkao area of Tamenglong district, approached by road from Tamenglong town.
practical_notes: The exact approach is not well signposted; confirm the route with local people before travelling.

name: Khoupum Valley
description: Khoupum is the second largest valley in Manipur, inhabited by the Rongmei community. The valley holds a large earthen dam, rivers, the Khukdai cave and a natural waterfall called Khouduang that has become a popular picnic spot.
how_to_reach: On the Old Cachar Road, about 81 km from Imphal, in Noney district.
practical_notes: The dam, cave and Khouduang waterfall are the main sights spread across the valley.

name: Integrated Tourist Destination, Tupul
description: The Integrated Tourist Destination at Tupul was inaugurated in January 2018 with the aim of developing Noney district as an off-beat destination. It lies close to the site of the major railway bridge project in the district.
how_to_reach: At Tupul in Noney district, about 64 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: An emerging destination with facilities still developing; check locally what is open.
address: Integrated Tourist Destination, Tupul, Noney, Manipur

name: Khuga Dam
description: Khuga Dam is a multipurpose dam just south of Churachandpur town at Mata village, built on the Khuga river. Construction began in 1983, resumed in 2002 and the dam was inaugurated in 2010; it stands 38 metres high and extends over about 230 metres.
how_to_reach: About 3 km from Churachandpur town. The nearest airport is Imphal Tulihal, with Dimapur and Jiribam as railheads.
practical_notes: A well-loved local picnic spot for its reservoir and hill views; the dam is not yet working to full capacity.

name: Ngaloi Waterfall
description: Ngaloi Waterfall is beside the small village of Ngaloi, whose original name is Ngaloimoul, about 9 km from Churachandpur. Low mountains and greenery frame the cascade as white, foamy water drops over dark rock.
how_to_reach: About 9 km from Churachandpur town at Ngaloimoul village; taxis and buses are available from town.
practical_notes: A manageable half-day trip from Churachandpur; the falls are most impressive during and after the rains.

name: Tonglon Cave
description: The Tonglon caves of Singngat sub-division are the best known caves in Churachandpur. Carvings, sculptures and engraved scripts in the caves offer historians and visitors a glimpse of early settlement and the district's past.
how_to_reach: In Singngat sub-division, about 10 km from Churachandpur town.
practical_notes: A torch and sturdy footwear are useful; the inscriptions are the main point of interest.

name: Manipur Mountaineering Institute (MMI), Lamdan
description: The foundation stone of the Manipur Mountaineering Institute at Lamdan was laid by Tenzing Norgay in 1985. Set over roughly 250 hectares, the institute promotes adventure and eco-tourism activities under the motto Aim High.
how_to_reach: At Lamdan in Churachandpur district, about 63 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: A base for trekking and rock-based adventure; contact the institute in advance about courses and expeditions.
address: Manipur Mountaineering Institute (MMI), Lamdan, Churachandpur, Manipur

name: Luipi Waterfall
description: Luipi Waterfall is a scenic and adventure-rated site in Pherzawl district, reached through hill country on NH 2. The district administration lists it as roughly 28 km from Pherzawl and about 163 km from Churachandpur.
how_to_reach: About 28 km from Pherzawl town via NH 2; the nearest airport is Imphal Tulihal and the nearest railhead Dimapur or Jiribam.
practical_notes: A remote waterfall, so arrange transport and provisions before setting out.

name: Yangoupokpi-Lokchao Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Yangoupokpi-Lokchao is a wildlife sanctuary of about 184.8 square kilometres on the Indo-Myanmar border in Chandel district, declared a sanctuary in 1989. Its forests represent the meeting of Indian and Burmese biodiversity and shelter species such as the hoolock gibbon, the only ape found in India, along with bears, leopards and migratory elephants.
how_to_reach: On the Indo-Myanmar border in Chandel district, about 110 km from Imphal, near Moreh.
practical_notes: October to April is the recommended season, and early morning is the best time for wildlife; entry may require permission from the forest department.

name: Bro Waterfall
description: Bro Waterfall is a hill waterfall in the Chandel area documented in E-Pao's Landscape and Loktak photo archive, which records a visit to the falls in October 2011.
how_to_reach: In Chandel district; the town of Chandel is the nearest mapped reference point for the approach.
practical_notes: A lesser-known natural site with limited signage; confirm the route and access locally before travelling.

name: Moreh
description: Moreh is a busy commercial town on the Indo-Myanmar border in Tengnoupal district, about 110 km from Imphal. It is a gateway to south-east Asia and a shopper's paradise, with goods ranging from electronics to everyday supplies, and a place to encounter Burmese culture across the border at Tamu, about 5 km away.
how_to_reach: About 110 km from Imphal on the Indo-Myanmar border in Tengnoupal district.
practical_notes: A border town: carry valid identification and check the current crossing rules. Hotels are available in town.

name: Kwatha Heritage Village
description: Kwatha is a village in Tengnoupal district on the edge of the Yangoupokpi-Lokchao Wildlife Sanctuary area, part of the border landscape where Manipuri and Burmese ecosystems meet.
how_to_reach: In Tengnoupal district near the Myanmar border, reached by road from the Imphal-Moreh route.
practical_notes: A border village with limited facilities; check local conditions and permissions before visiting.

name: Liabi Waterfall
description: Liabi Waterfall lies in the forest of Chatric and Siyang villages in Kamjong district and is listed by the district administration as a natural and scenic site.
how_to_reach: About 40 km from Kamjong headquarters, partly connected by the Ukhrul-Kamjong state highway; the nearest airport is Imphal, about 120 km away.
practical_notes: A taxi or private vehicle is needed; the nearest major railhead is Dimapur in Nagaland, roughly 318 km away.

name: Ningshing Khun
description: Ningshing Khun village in Jiribam district contains a biodiversity park and a memorial complex honouring the heroes Bir Tikendrajit, General Thangal and Paona Brajabashi.
how_to_reach: At Ningshing Khun in Jiribam district, about 201 km from Imphal.
practical_notes: The memorial and the biodiversity park together make up the visit; it is a long trip from Imphal.

name: Manipur State Museum
description: Manipur State Museum sits near the polo ground in Imphal and displays the state's tribal heritage alongside portraits of former rulers. Its collections include costumes, arms and weapons, relics and historical documents.
how_to_reach: Near the polo ground in Imphal; the district page lists Tulihal International Airport as the nearest airport and Dimapur railway station as the nearest railhead.
practical_notes: Open 10 am to 4.30 pm; closed on Mondays and holidays.
address: Manipur State Museum, Imphal West, Manipur

name: Nupi Lal Memorial Complex
description: The Nupi Lal Memorial Complex honours Manipuri women who sacrificed their lives fighting for justice against the British on 12 December 1939.
how_to_reach: In Imphal; the district page lists Tulihal International Airport as the nearest airport and Dimapur railway station as the nearest railhead.
practical_notes: The official district page gives no entry-fee or timing details; check locally before visiting.
address: Nupi Lal Memorial Complex, Imphal West, Manipur

name: Thangjing Temple
description: Moirang, about 45 km from Imphal, is a sacred place for the Manipuri people and holds an ancient temple of the pre-Hindu deity Lord Thangjing. The traditional Moirang Lai Haraoba is celebrated in May, when men and women sing and dance in honour of Thangjing.
how_to_reach: In Moirang, about 45 km from Imphal; Moirang Bazar is the local bus stop named by the district page.
practical_notes: The district page notes the annual Lai Haraoba in May; visitors should respect temple customs.

name: Bishnupur Vishnu Temple
description: Bishnupur, 27 km from Imphal on Tiddim Road, is home to a conical Vishnu temple built in 1467 during the reign of King Kyamba. The district page notes its antiquity and architectural design influenced by Chinese style; the town is also known for stoneware.
how_to_reach: About 27 km from Imphal on Tiddim Road; the district page lists Tulihal Airport in Imphal and Jiribam railway station as the nearest air and rail points.
practical_notes: The official district page gives no entry-fee details; check locally.

name: Makhel
description: Makhel is a sacred place for many ethnic communities who believe their ancestors settled there and migrated from it long ago. The Senapati district page lists historical monuments including sacred banyan trees said to have grown from the tomb of the Naga mother, a farewell monolith and a dispersal tree at Sajouba.
how_to_reach: Makhel is listed among the places of interest in Senapati district; check the exact village approach locally.
practical_notes: The sacred monuments are spread around the village rather than gathered at a single entrance; check local directions on arrival.

name: Singda Dam
description: Singda is a picnic spot about 16 km from Imphal beside an artificial lake associated with Kangchup. The state's dam report says the earthen Singda Dam across the Singda River was completed in 1995 and supplies irrigation, 0.75 MW of hydropower and domestic water.
how_to_reach: In the Singda and Kangchup area west of Imphal; the state tourism page describes the picnic spot and its artificial lake.
practical_notes: The state page notes an inspection bungalow at Singda; check current visitor access and room availability locally.

name: Khayang Waterfall
description: Khayang (Tililytiluelue) Waterfall lies in the forest of Khayang village in Kamjong district and is listed by the district administration as a natural and scenic site.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from Kamjong headquarters; the district page recommends hiring a taxi or using a self-driven vehicle. Imphal airport is about 120 km away and Dimapur is the nearest major railhead.
practical_notes: The district page says to hire a taxi or use a self-driven vehicle; confirm road and access conditions locally.

name: Hundung Mova Cave
description: Hundung Mova Cave is a limestone cave near the defunct cement factory and Lungshang Kong river in a small hamlet called Hungpung. The district page says its main hall can assemble more than 100 people.
how_to_reach: About 15 km from Ukhrul headquarters on the Imphal-Ukhrul route on NH150; a taxi or self vehicle can be hired.
practical_notes: The district page links a steep rock mountain near the cave with the cave in local myth; check access locally before entering.

name: Barak River
description: The Pherzawl district page lists the Barak (Tuiruong) among the district's important rivers. Ruonglevaisuo, the confluence of the Tuivai and Barak, is an important business hub and port for local boats carrying goods and people along the river.
how_to_reach: The district page places the Barak River area about 63 km from Pherzawl district headquarters via NH2.
practical_notes: This record is for the Barak river landscape at Pherzawl, distinct from Barak Waterfalls in Tamenglong district.

name: Noney Railway Bridge
description: The Noney district page describes the bridge as a 141-metre-tall railway pier bridge on the 111-km Jiribam-Imphal project, calling it the world's tallest railway pier bridge. It says the 703-metre bridge crosses the Aling river and that the work is being undertaken by North East Frontier Railway.
how_to_reach: In Noney district on the Jiribam-Imphal railway alignment; the district page gives no road approach details.
practical_notes: An engineering landmark; the official page reports construction status and dimensions that may change, so check current access locally.

name: Langol Peak Garden
description: Langol Peak Garden, also called Tlanglhungbung Leikol, lies in Langol village in Machi Sub-Division of Chandel district. The district page links the peak in legend to Thoibi gathering Thoibi-Lei flowers and says Allied forces camped there during the Second World War.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from central Imphal along the Indo-Myanmar road; the district lists AH2 as the road route.
practical_notes: The district describes landscaped hillocks and scenery; check local conditions before travelling.
